subject: Private VPC proxy fabric & tenant bisection review
messages:

To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, DataWave Systems <infra@datwave.example.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-21T08:12:00Z
Subject: Private VPC proxy fabric & tenant bisection review

Hi all,

Attached is the first-pass reference diagram for the private VPC deployment at DataWave (dw-proxy-fabric-v1.pdf). The goal for this thread is to validate the proxy fabric and tenant bisection model before we lock routing and NAT assumptions. High-level asks:

- Can DataWave confirm whether the on-prem edge will terminate TLS on the Diva DataCenter load balancer or hand TLS through to our proxy?
- Rishi/Naomi: please call out any KV-cache/forwarding implications of the proposed sidecar vs. centralized proxy.
- Ops: confirm required egress IP ranges and whether secondary NAT pools are available for burst traffic.

Key constraints we know today: the deployment must preserve tenant bisection (no cross-tenant flows), allow short-lived burst capacity to public nets, and maintain a 50ms added latency SLO from edge to inference nodes.

Next steps: review comments by EOD Wed (2027-09-22). If we get alignment, Stephanie will produce an annotated diagram and runbook.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dw-proxy-fabric-v1.pdf (diagram), tenant-isolation-matrix.xlsx (matrix stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private VPC proxy fabric & tenant bisection review

Lauren — quick pass from the serving/runtime side. A few technical notes and risks:

1) Sidecar vs centralized proxy
   - Sidecar (per-tenant proxy) simplifies tenant bisection and local KV cache affinity, but increases connection counts and makes TLS termination per-node necessary.
   - Centralized proxy cluster reduces connection surface and lets us keep a single KV cache slice, but we must guarantee strict network ACLs to prevent east-west cross-tenant traffic.

2) KV cache warming and cold-starts
   - If the proxy performs prefix caching, ensure consistent affinity hashing so that cache misses don't route across tenant boundaries. Recommend sticky hashing keyed to tenant-id + model-shard.

3) Egress/NAT
   - We need explicit /29 pools for each tenant's control-plane callbacks (audit logs) so downstream services can allowlist. If DataWave can't provide per-tenant pools, we'll need to implement application-level source tagging and a proxy-level ACL translate which complicates logging and may impact throughput.

I left inline comments on dw-proxy-fabric-v1.pdf (see pdf annotations).

-Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: DataWave Systems <infra@datwave.example.com>

Date: 2027-09-22T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Private VPC proxy fabric & tenant bisection review

Thanks, Lauren and team. Couple of clarifications from our side:

- TLS termination: our preferred pattern is TLS passthrough to Redwood's proxy (we terminate at your sidecar/central cluster). Diva DataCenter can provide L4 load balancing with SNI.
- NAT pools: we can allocate two /29 pools initially; we'll need to reserve a third for compliance auditing. We'll confirm allocation by tomorrow.
- Physical demarc: Diva will install the edge appliance in rack 12B; Diva ops will share crossconnect details after we sign off.

Two requests from DataWave:
1) Can you confirm what CVE-level kernel/openssl versions your sidecar depends on (security wants a CVE-compatible list)?
2) We need a brief runbook for failover: if the central proxy cluster gets overloaded, what happens to new session establishment?

We reviewed your attachment and added a short set of notes; will upload an annotated PDF (ops annotations) after NAT confirmation.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Infrastructure Lead, DataWave Systems

Attachments: - (placeholder for Diva/Diva-crossconnect.pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: DataWave Systems <infra@datwave.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T17:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Private VPC proxy fabric & tenant bisection review

Thanks Samir — answering the two asks and proposing acceptance criteria/next actions.

Answers:
- CVE/kernel list: see attached dw-proxy-fabric-v2-annotated.pdf page 3 (runtime dependencies) and the short package list below. We'll provide the full SBOM after we finalize the artifact build.
  - OpenSSL 3.1.2 or later (patched), linux kernel 5.15+ (backported patches as required), musl/gcc runtime libs pinned to our build.

- Failover runbook (summary):
  - New sessions: if central proxy cluster is at >75% CPU, new TCP connections are drained to standby cluster in a different AZ (active-passive).
  - Sidecar pattern: if sidecars are used, traffic will continue locally; control-plane will rate-limit model loads to protect KV cache.
  - Fallback: automated routing policy will prefer smallest-additional-latency path; we will surface metrics to your ops dashboard and trigger PagerDuty if >5% request failures for 10 minutes.

Acceptance criteria to close this review:
1) DataWave confirms TLS passthrough and provides NAT pools (/29 x2) by 2027-09-23 EOD.
2) Diva crossconnect details shared and validated.
3) We produce final annotated diagram + operations runbook (deliverable target: 2027-09-26).

I've attached the annotated PDF and an updated tenant-isolation-matrix.xlsx with rows for NAT mapping and audit endpoints.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Technical Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dw-proxy-fabric-v2-annotated.pdf, tenant-isolation-matrix.xlsx

Team — quick summary and acceptance:

- DataWave confirmed TLS passthrough and committed two /29 NAT pools; Diva to confirm crossconnect timeline (Samir to share link).
- Rishi: we accepted sidecar fallback for hot-paths and central proxy for baseline traffic — please capture the affinity hashing recommendation in the runbook.
- Naomi/Stephanie: please finalize the annotated diagrams and the runbook; set up a 30-minute walk-through with DataWave next week (Sep 28).

I'll mark this review as 'accepted-pending-runbook' and attach the final set of artifacts once Stephanie uploads them. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Lauren

Redwood Inference
